templates.text: Sudden head tilt → immediate asymmetric tonic neck reflex, contralateral arm extends.
Passive leg extension → rapid recoil to flexion, followed by a vigorous Moro fragment.
Deep pressure on sole → powerful plantar grasp, hip and knee flexion pulling against stimulus.
Abrupt trunk rotation → strong body-righting response, limbs reorganizing to face new orientation.
Sustained palmar touch → firm grasp, whole-arm flexion, and a sharp inspiratory gasp.
Sudden loss of support → full Moro reflex: arm abduction, cry onset in under {seconds} second.
Nose/mouth obstruction → forceful head turn, arm swipe, and a loud, expulsive cry.
Restraint of limbs → strong, rhythmic struggling motions against the hold, face reddens.
Tactile stimulus to cheek → immediate rooting, head turn, and mouth opening in one fluid motion.
Sudden loud noise → startle, eye blink, and a brief, high-pitched cry before self-quieting.
Gentle sway interrupted → limbs stiffen, then a burst of stepping movements to regain equilibrium.
Pressure on foot during flexion → strong Babinski sign, toes fan and dorsiflex.
Lateral tilt of bassinet → body arches toward the higher side, arms reach for stability.
Light touch to corner of mouth → head rotates, lips purse, and tongue extends in search.
Sudden bright light → eyes squeeze shut, head jerks back, hands fly up toward face.
Firm stroking along spine → Galant reflex: trunk curves concavely toward the stimulus side.
Brief restraint of breathing → powerful extension of trunk and neck, followed by a deep, recovery gasp.
Sustained prone position → attempts at head lift, alternating leg movements as if crawling.
Sudden temperature change → whole-body shudder, cry, then frantic limb movement to generate heat.
Palmar grasp pulled gently → grip tightens reflexively, shoulder muscles engage to resist release.
Nostril lightly touched → head turns away sharply, hand makes a swatting motion near the face.
Heel pressed firmly → leg withdraws in flexion, then extends forcefully in a kick.
Abdominal pressure in prone → pelvis lifts, crawling movements initiate with coordinated limb alternation.
Sudden downward motion → arms splay wide, fingers spread, a sharp cry is elicited.
Continuous touch on lower back → hip elevates on the stimulated side in a clear pelvic tilt.
Mouth stimulus during cry → immediate suckling motion interrupts cry for {seconds} seconds.
Constraint around chest → arching back, pushing with feet, and crying with increased pitch.
Unexpected tilt to left → right arm and leg extend in a protective parachute-like response.
Simulated fall sensation → gasp, eyes widen, full body startle with vocalization.
Rhythmic pat on back → crying ceases, body relaxes into the rhythm, limbs go limp.
